pages.text: The crank only reads the $(item)Machine Input$() directly below it. That input takes rotation on its shaft side, like any Create component, and nothing else can drive the crank.$(br2)Each tick, the base pumps:

$(item)RPM x (connector distance / 5) x sin(crank angle)$() mB$(br2)$(li)$(item)RPM$() is the speed of the machine input, in either direction.$(li)$(item)Connector distance$() is the number of blocks between the holder and the connector along the beam.
$(li)The sine follows the stroke, so the flow pulses: highest mid-stroke, zero at the top and bottom. On average you get about $(item)two thirds$() of the peak.
Example: the pumpjack on the first page has its connector 3 blocks from the holder. At 64 RPM it peaks at about 38 mB per tick, roughly $(item)490 mB per second$() on average.
To pump faster, spin the input faster or move the connector further from the holder. The machine input has a stress impact of $(item)4 per RPM$(), so 64 RPM costs 256 SU.
